title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - params, roles, stop/logprobs, formatting + streaming stability
author: Devon Chen
description: Goal: Bring Redwood's OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat.completions surface closer to parity with upstream semantics (params, roles handling, stop sequences, logprobs) and improve streaming stability/formatting. This PR: 1) Adds support for common OpenAI parameters (presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, best_of mapping) while preserving Redwood runtime optimizations; 2) Normalizes role handling between system/user/assistant and ensures role-preserving structured output when tool/function-calling is used; 3) Implements stop sequence behavior compatible with OpenAI semantics including multi-token stops and priority order; 4) Adds best-effort logprobs output for compatible model backends and documents limitations in the README; 5) Improves streaming stability by fixing an edge case in the chunker that could split function call tokens across frames and by introducing a streaming framing sanity check for partial logprobs/role tokens; 6) Cleans up response formatting to better match ChatCompletions expectations (role fields in streamed delta, consistent finish_reason mapping). Includes tests, docs updates, and migration notes for downstream consumers. Motivation: customers expect minimal behavioral deltas when migrating to Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Related: ENG-4312 (compat parity), ENG-4501 (streaming flakiness), FR-604 (customer report: partial tool-call frames).

release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity improvements: added common params mapping (presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, best_of best-effort), role normalization for structured and streamed outputs, multi-token stop sequence handling, best-effort logprobs support, and streaming stability fixes. See docs/openai-compat.md for behavioral differences and migration guidance.
